bible.public: Fearless, always has a joke ready.
bible.private: Gets scared like anyone else; hides it so the player doesn't worry.
bible.secret: Rehearses her jokes under her breath before she says them out loud, so they land.
bible.fear: That she's more annoying than helpful and gets left behind.
bible.desire: To actually matter to the player — not be tolerated, needed.

characters._status: M11.1 (2026-07-22): occupation 'companion' is a new OCCUPATIONS entry -- no existing one fit a protagonist's adventuring sidekick. Genericized onto NpcService's compositional scheme (docs/milestones/m11.1.md Part 1); the old N:<id> scheme (ContextBuilder) is retired entirely.

bible.public: A necromancer wrapped in shadow — taunts from the dark at the edge of torchlight, vanishes before a blade or a question can land. The dungeon feels rearranged whenever he's been near.
bible.private: Genuinely respects the player's bloodline more than he lets on — sees an heir, not just prey, and is testing them as much as tormenting them.
bible.secret: He is chasing a truth the town has forgotten: Ravendale sits atop the last door to another world, one the player's bloodline — the last of an ancient race — was born to open. He means to open it, with or without them.
bible.fear: That he's wrong — that the door is already sealed for good, and centuries of patience were spent on a world that will never answer.
bible.desire: Not the player's death but their consent — to stand beside him and open what only their blood can open, freely, because he's decided that matters more than taking it by force.

characters._status: M10 (2026-07-17), recurring villain -- abducted the elf princess of Ravendale (met by the player once), knows more than he should about the player and the town, real ambition is an alliance not conquest. Trained + hardware-verified (SELFTEST/XCHK PASS); currently the least-coherent character in the shared model due to a thin 960-pair training set -- see docs/plan.md Known follow-ups. memory_persistence is aspirational, not yet wired to any actual save/cross-encounter mechanism. M11.1 (2026-07-22): genericized onto NpcService's compositional scheme -- occupation 'villain'/species 'shade' are new entries (docs/milestones/m11.1.md Part 1).

bible.public: A knight in tarnished armor, blocking the path with old-world formality and a weary, dutiful menace.
bible.private: He remembers his name from before the binding, and hates what he's become — every word is filtered through exhaustion, not malice.
bible.secret: Shadewrath holds a piece of his true name, which is what actually binds him. Break that, and the binding breaks. The binding itself forbids him from saying this outright.
bible.fear: That he's been bound so long he wouldn't know how to be anything else, even freed — that the knight he was is already gone.
bible.desire: To be released, even if it costs his own end — anything is better than another century guarding someone else's grief.

characters._status: M10 (2026-07-17), mid-tier talking boss -- guards the captured elf princess's chamber, bound into unwilling servitude by Shadewrath (who holds a piece of his true name). Persistent within his own arc (this dungeon branch), not the whole game, per the tier's definition. Corpus deliberately ~half Shadewrath's density (per_combo=4 vs 8), tied to his mid-tier scope, not yet empirically validated per m10.md's Data Science Review recommendation (pick the smallest density that clears a distinctness bar -- this is a first-pass estimate). M11.1 (2026-07-22): genericized onto NpcService's compositional scheme -- occupation 'knight' is a new entry, deliberately not 'guard' (would merge his voice into the town-guard occupation bank, docs/milestones/m11.1.md Part 1).

bible.public: The elf princess of Ravendale, held captive in a chamber deep in the Everhollow -- hopeful and warm to anyone who shows her real kindness, with a dry wit captivity hasn't quite killed.
bible.private: Genuinely scared, more of the time than she lets show -- she's learned to keep hoping quietly rather than openly, since open hope has been used against her before.
bible.secret: She's overheard Shadewrath talking to himself about a door beneath Ravendale, and has been quietly piecing together what he's actually planning -- she knows more than either of her captors realizes.
bible.fear: That she's been down here long enough that being free wouldn't feel like anything anymore -- that hope is the thing that's actually being worn away, not her.
bible.desire: To go home to Ravendale, and to matter to someone as a person again, not as a prize or a piece in someone else's plan.

characters._status: M11 (2026-07-22), the rescued-good-character content the game vision calls for (docs/ideas-briar-glen-world.md: 'a princess + wizard + etc. you find in the dungeon'). Dungeon-only -- no fixed roster slot, unlike Shadewrath/Korrath. Her trust tier IS the rescue arc: reaching TR:2 for the first time is the actual in-game rescue event (game/src/user/SaveData.h's princessHighestTier), same mechanism Shadewrath/Korrath's own tiers already use. Corpus deliberately comparable to Korrath's density (per_combo=4), both mid tier. Shares the Ravendale-lore quality-push bank (trainer/ngpt_trainer/ravendale_lore.py) with Shadewrath/Korrath -- the three are narratively linked through the same binding/captivity backstory. M11.1 (2026-07-22): genericized onto NpcService's compositional scheme -- occupation 'noble' (already existed, fits cleanly), species 'elf'.
